question: On 26 October 2026, the US military banned BYD vehicles from its military facilities, following the adoption of similar measures in Poland, the United Kingdom and Israel. Most vehicles are now equipped with cameras, LiDAR, GPS and microphones that can capture and film sensitive information and transmit it to the carmaker.

In Norway, soldiers discovered that Chinese vehicles rented during a military exercise had filmed both them and the access codes to military installations. Moreover, China’s 2017 national intelligence law requires companies to cooperate with the state. Allowing connected vehicles from third countries to access sensitive European infrastructure therefore poses an unacceptable security risk.
Given this, does the Commission intend to: 1.

refer the matter to the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) to assess the threat and, where appropriate, include BYD in the list of high-risk suppliers under Article 104 of the proposed regulation on ENISA, the European cybersecurity certification framework and ICT supply chain security1 and/or impose restrictions on the import of BYD vehicles into the EU?
restrict Chinese vehicles’ access to strategic dual-use infrastructure through an implementing act, as referred to in Article 34(4) of the proposed regulation on military mobility2?
exclude BYD from public procurement under Article 66 of the proposed EU public procurement act3?

Commission proposal of 20 January 2026 for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), the European cybersecurity certification framework, and ICT supply chain security and repealing Regulation (EU) 2019/881 (The Cybersecurity Act 2) (COM(2026)0011).

2 Commission proposal of 19 November 2025 for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on establishing a framework of measures to facilitate the transport of military equipment, goods and personnel across the Union (COM(2025)0847).

3 Commission proposal of 9 September 2026 for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on public contracts and concessions, repealing Directives 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU, and amending Regulations (EC) No 1370/2007, (EU) 2023/1542, (EU) 2024/1157, (EU) 2024/1252, (EU) 2024/1735, (EU) 2024/1781, (EU) 2024/2847, (EU) 2024/3110 and (EU) 2025/40, and Directives 2008/98/EC, (EU) 2019/882, (EU) 2022/2381, (EU) 2023/1791 and (EU) 2024/1760 (Public Procurement Act) (COM(2026)0590).
